subject: Liability cap: recovery hurdle proposal & annual reset mechanics
messages:
From: Sarah Collins <sarah.collins@bluepeak.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Intro — liability cap / recovery-hurdle concept

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the latency numbers. Our GC and procurement teams asked for a short note on the liability cap mechanics we discussed on the call. Attached is the template BluePeak legal normally uses for LOli (limitation of liability) and a short summary of the commercial ask.

High-level ask from our side: we need a hard monetary cap but want an annual reset rather than a single contract-term aggregate; we also want a carve-out for data breach remediation and a notion of a "recovery hurdle" (first-loss threshold we cover before the aggregate cap applies). The goal is to protect both sides while keeping an operationally simple SOW.

Questions for Redwood:
- Would you consider a 1x annualized-fees cap with a 90-day recovery-hurdle of $250k for first-loss items?
- Can certain categories (statutory fines, third-party IP indemnity) remain carve-outs?
- If we agree to an annual reset, are there reporting hooks where you can surface billing-year fees in the console for audit?

I've copied Marissa for legal coordination. Happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Thanks,
Sarah Collins
Head of Procurement, BluePeak Analytics
Attachments: BP_LOLI_Appendix_v2.docx (docx)

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Collins <sarah.collins@bluepeak.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro — liability cap / recovery-hurdle concept

Sarah — really helpful framing, thanks. Quick responses inline below and in short: we can get close, but need a couple of guardrails so the cap remains insurable and predictable for our SRE/runbook obligations.

On the numbers: a 1x annual-fees baseline is within the range we typically accept for mid-market customers. The recovery-hurdle idea is new but interesting — operationally it would act like a small first-loss bucket that BluePeak absorbs, with Redwood liability kicking in after that amount per incident or per billing year (we should be explicit).

My ask back to you: could we split the recovery-hurdle into two dimensions: (a) per-incident first-loss of $100k, and (b) an annual aggregate first-loss of $250k, beyond which the 1x annual fees cap would apply? That keeps the per-event exposure bounded for both sides.

Carve-outs: statutory fines and third-party IP indemnities are standard carve-outs for us as well. We would also request a carve-out for customer-driven misuse or prompt-engineering modifications that fall outside our documented use cases.

Reporting: we can expose a billing-year summary in the Console and provide a quarter-end export link for audit. I copied Karthik (legal) to propose redline language and Laura (commercial) to confirm how this maps to billing windows for the order form.

Proposed next step: Marissa / Karthik to send a redline with the per-incident and annual-first-loss phrasing. If you prefer, we can also propose a short three-way call Friday to finalize.

Cheers,
Alex Martinez
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Collins <sarah.collins@bluepeak.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood redline — proposed language for recovery hurdle and annual reset (attached)

Sarah / Alex,

Please find attached a redline version of the MSA section and an accompanying spreadsheet that models different cap outcomes under (i) per-incident first-loss + annual-first-loss, (ii) pure per-contract aggregate, and (iii) per-billing-window caps. Key points in the redline:

- Definition: "Recovery Hurdle" — the amount of Customer-incurred loss that must be satisfied on a per-incident or per-year basis before Redwood's cap applies. We proposed both a per-incident and annual component to give symmetrical protection.
- Cap: Redwood proposes Liability Cap = the greater of (a) 1x fees paid in the prior 12 months, or (b) $500k; this floor keeps smaller deals insurable.
- Annual reset: caps reset on the anniversary of the effective date on a rolling 12-month basis tied to fees billed in the prior 12 months.
- Carve-outs: expressly carve out (i) statutory fines and penalties, (ii) third-party IP claims subject to indemnity, (iii) willful misconduct, and (iv) obligations under binding court order.
- Remedy flow: for incidents involving customer data exposure, we proposed a banded remediation-first approach: Redwood covers remediation costs up to the per-incident recovery hurdle; if cumulative remediation in a 12-month window exceeds the annual-first-loss, Redwood's liability is capped per the Cap rule above.

I flagged places where BluePeak's original template diverged materially from our preferred language. See column comments in the spreadsheet.

Attachments: redline-msa-recovery-hurdle.xlsx (xlsx), BP_LOLI_Appendix_v2.docx (docx)

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Collins <sarah.collins@bluepeak.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood redline — quick note on indemnity / scope and next steps

Sarah — thanks for reviewing. Couple of clarifications from legal ops:

1) Scope: The proposed per-incident/annual-first-loss approach is acceptable to Redwood's underwriters assuming the floor ($500k) remains. If BluePeak prefers a lower floor, we'd need conduit approvals and would expect premium trade-offs (e.g., higher renewal-based credit or narrower carve-outs).

2) Billing-data hook: Alex confirmed we'll provide a CSV export from the Console showing fees paid per 12-month rolling window. We'll also add a doc reference in the order form that points to the HubSpot deal record for auditing purposes.

3) Drafting note: substitute "annual-first-loss" for "annual recovery-hurdle" in the MSA to reduce ambiguity. Example snip we will use in the MSA: "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, Customer shall be responsible for the first $100,000 per claim and the first $250,000 in the aggregate per rolling 12-month period (the "Annual First-Loss"), after which Redwood's liability shall be subject to the Liability Cap set forth below."

Next steps: Marissa will send a tracked redline back to BluePeak legal with the alternate floor scenarios called out; if BluePeak is comfortable we can convert to an order-form clause that maps to fees-billed windows. If BluePeak wants the floor lowered, we'll coordinate an underwriter exception and return with a term sheet.

Karthik Iyer
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference
